sources.quote: I now like Arnaldo: he was Armando's greatest friend, but the friendship is over.
sources.context: Wilde to Robert Ross, Rome, April 1900, in the sentence immediately after giving up Armando. The whole of the record for Arnaldo.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: That Wilde replaced one young Roman with his best friend, and said so plainly.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 1228; printed folio 1182 confirmed on the rendered page image.

name: Arnaldo
bio: A young Roman, Armando's closest friend, whom Wilde took up in April 1900 when he gave Armando up. He survives in one sentence: 'I now like Arnaldo: he was Armando's greatest friend, but the friendship is over.'
bio_note: The gap existed because only Armando has his own General Index entry ('Armando (boy), 1182, 1184'); the other two appear inside the same paragraphs and are indexed nowhere.
